facts.statement: Changzhousaurus fossils were found in the Jiufotang Formation in western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The Changzhousaurus fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Jiufotang Formation in Lamadong of Jianchang County in western Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: Changzhousaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian) period.
facts.quote: Age: Early Cretaceous (Aptian)

facts.statement: Changzhousaurus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Changzhousaurus had large wings on its forelimbs and shorter wings on its hindlimbs.
facts.quote: It has large wings on its forelimbs, paired with shorter hindlimb wings.

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Changzhousaurus had four unserrated teeth, with the second being the largest.
facts.quote: The premaxillae have four unserrated teeth, the second of which is the largest.

facts.statement: The maxilla contained around fifteen unserrated teeth following the premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: These are followed by around fifteen teeth in the maxilla, all of which also lack serrations.

facts.statement: Changzhousaurus likely had around 20 teeth, with front teeth being slender and close together, while rear teeth were robust and widely spaced.
facts.quote: It likely bore around 20 teeth, with those at the front more slender and close together compared to the more robust, widely spaced ones at the rear of the jaw.

facts.statement: Nine cervical vertebrae were identified in the holotype, though ten were likely present.
facts.quote: Nine cervical (neck) vertebrae were identified in the C. sinensis holotype, though ten were likely present.

facts.statement: The forelimb was proportionately long, about 60% the length of the hindlimb.
facts.quote: The forelimb is proportionately long, similar to Xiaotingia, about 60% the length of the hindlimb.

facts.statement: The enlarged pedal claw on the second digit was 7.5 mm long, with a keratin sheath adding another 4.5 mm.
facts.quote: The enlarged pedal ungual II is 7.5 mm long, with the sheath adding an additional 4.5 mm.

facts.statement: Feathers on the body ranged from 10 to 35 mm in length over the head and neck.
facts.quote: On the body, the feathers range from 10 - 35 mm over the head and neck.

facts.statement: Feathers from the base to the center of the tail were 20 to 30 mm long.
facts.quote: From the base of the tail to its center, the feathers are 20 - 30 mm long.

facts.statement: About 16 long feathers were visible at the tail tip, similar to those in early-diverging avialans and some scansoriopterygids.
facts.quote: About 16 long feathers are visible at the tip of the tail, comparable to those seen in many early-diverging avialans and some scansoriopterygids.

facts.statement: Hindlimb feathers ranged from 25 to 35 mm on the femur and tibia, up to 60 mm on the metatarsals.
facts.quote: The hindlimb feathers range from 25 - 35 mm long on the femur and tibia, to 60 mm on the metatarsals.

facts.statement: Changzhousaurus is classified as a pennaraptoran theropod with a mosaic of features, possibly an early-diverging deinonychosaurian.
facts.quote: A pennaraptoran theropod with an unusual mosaic of features; possibly an early-diverging deinonychosaurian.

facts.statement: Xu (2026) placed Changzhousaurus within Deinonychosauria as an early-diverging member to support the monophyly of that group.
facts.quote: Xu (2026) used this unique combination of traits to support the monophyly of Deinonychosauria, within which he preferred an early-diverging placement for Changzhousaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether dromaeosaurids and troodontids form a single monophyletic clade called Deinonychosauria.
facts.quote: Some researchers group dromaeosaurids and troodontids into a single monophyletic clade, the Deinonychosauria, but this is not supported by all analyses.

facts.statement: The holotype individual was likely not a juvenile but was not fully mature when it died.
facts.quote: The fusion of the sacral vertebrae suggests this individual was not a juvenile, though the lack of fusion between the metatarsals and distal tarsals (those furthest from the body) suggests it was not yet fully mature when it died.

facts.statement: The femur was bowed anteriorly and shorter than the tibia.
facts.quote: The femur (upper leg bone) is bowed anteriorly (toward the front), and shorter than the tibia (shin bone).

facts.statement: Keratin sheath impressions are preserved around the hand and foot claws of the holotype.
facts.quote: Keratin sheath impressions are preserved around both the hand and foot ungual of the holotype.
